dossiers.catalyst_stack: On April 2 and June 30, 2026, Transocean stacked about $2 billion of harsh-environment and Brazil/Norway backlog through the Vår Energi/Petrobras fixtures and the Equinor Cat D package, then added Eastern Mediterranean, ONGC India, and Equatorial Guinea awards through September 29. August 5 Q2 results printed $966 million of contract drilling revenue, a beat versus estimates, $6.7 billion backlog, and a FY2026 revenue guidance raise to $3.900–$3.975 billion. The Valaris path improved with CFIUS approval on June 29, DOJ Second Request certification on August 25, and September 21 reports of an early no-divestiture clearance, while a September 24 SDNY ruling dismissed the securities class action with leave to amend. Offsetting that, May 4 DOJ Second Requests and Brazil CADE’s August 7 full-form review still gate the combination, and Barclays and Susquehanna cut price targets to $7 in July–August.
dossiers.key_assumption: The Equinor Cat D licenses are approved and the Valaris combination closes without a DOJ or CADE block or forced divestitures, so the backlog and merger-synergy thesis is realized rather than reversed.

dossiers.catalyst_stack: On 31 Aug 2026 SLB agreed to buy Kelvion for about $3.4 billion cash plus roughly $700 million of debt (close expected 1H 2027), after completing the Envirex subsea bolt-on (11 May), Tachyus (reported 24 Jul), and S&P Global’s upstream software portfolio (1 Sep). Contract momentum stayed intact with a seven-year Kuwait Oil Company AIV technology award (30 Jun), OQEP’s Bisat-B expansion to 548,000 bpd in Oman (23 Sep), and four multi-year Aramco well-construction packages (29 Sep), alongside a 14 Jul Liberty Energy data-center power alliance. Capital returns continued via a $0.295 quarterly dividend (23 Jul) and $648 million of Q2 buybacks (12 million shares, 24 Jul), while UBS lifted its target to $75 (14 Sep) and Rothschild to $68 (25 Sep). Offsets include Q1 Middle East disruptions that cut sequential revenue and margins (24 Apr), a $2 billion senior-notes issue (7 May), and CEO Olivier Le Peuch’s 35,000-share sale at $60 on 1 Sep.
dossiers.key_assumption: Kelvion closes on the stated 1H 2027 timetable without a leverage or synergy scare, and Middle East disruptions remain a contained sequential hit rather than a lasting NOC-capex cut that would mute the Aramco/KOC/Oman awards.

dossiers.key_assumption: Chart delivers the stated $325 million of year-three synergies and IET LNG/power backlog converts on schedule, rather than slipping on FIDs, permits, or turbine-capacity constraints that would unwind the FY 2026 guide.

dossiers.key_assumption: 2026 ounce/AISC guidance and the $6 billion buyback still hold after Cadia downtime, and gold does not break lower if real rates reprice higher.
